sentences.text: 2. By way of award dated 20.06.2013, the learned .

Tribunal has allowed the claim petition and awarded the following relief to the appellant: "In the light of what has been discussed here inabove while recording findings on issues of supra, the claim petition is allowed against respondents.

The respondents No.1 shall pay a compensation amount of `50,000/ to the petitioner on the basis of 'no fault liability rt under section 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 to be indemnified by respondent No.2, i.e. New India Assurance Company.
The amount of interim award, if any, shall be reduced from this final award.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties to the present lis are, hereinafter, referred to, in the same manner, as were, referred to, by the learned Tribunal.

4. Brief facts, leading to the filing of present appeal, before this Court, may be summed up as under: 4.1. PetitionerArvind Kumar, has filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V.
Act, for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/, along with interest @ 12% per annum, on account of death of his mother Smt. Lajja Devi in a road accident involving vehicle No HR38L0712 (hereinafter referred to as the 'offending vehicle'), against the respondents, being ownercum driver, as well as, Insurer of the offending vehicle, 4.2.

It is the further case of the petitioner that on .
14.4.2010, his mother was travelling in a car No.HP33B 2772, along with her daughter, sonin law and grand children, and was coming back from Haridwar, to their native place.

When, they reached near village Kalpi, District of Ambala, at about 3.30 p.m., then the offending vehicle, being driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, came rt there and hit the Car, in which the deceased was travelling.
4.3. Consequently, all the occupants, along with, the driver had expired.
The matter was reported to the police of Police Station, Mulana, District Ambala, Haryana.

Age of Smt. Lajja Devi, has been pleaded as 60 years and as per the case of the petitioner, she was getting pension of Rs.15,000/.
4.4
On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the petition, as prayed for.
5. When put to notice, the claim petition has been contested by the respondents.
6. Respondent No.1, has filed the reply, be denying the accident, in question.
It has also been pleaded that the respondent has wrongly arrayed Amrik Singh, as, respondent No.1, alleging to be the registered owner of the offending vehicle.

6.1. On merits, the contents of the claim petition have .
been denied by asserting the fact that the accident had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.HP33B2772.

Rest of the contents of the claim petition Arvind Kumar vs Sohan Singh And Another on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27553763/
2 have been denied.

sentences.text: While replying to the contents of paragraphs 22 and 24 of the claim petition, respondent No.1 has elaborated rt his stand that the driver of car bearing No.HP33B2772, was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner.
He had lost control over the car and struck the same against the offending vehicle.
However, due to the influence of the occupants of the car, the police of Police Station, Mulana, has registered the false case against him.

7. Respondent No.2Insurance Company, has filed its reply, by taking the preliminary objections that the offending vehicle was being permitted to ply, without valid and effective registration certificatecumfitness certificate and without valid route permit; that the petitioner is major and married son of the deceased, as such, he is not dependent upon the deceased; that the accident, in question, had taken place due to head on collision between the car bearing No.HP33B2772 and the offending vehicle; and that the driver of the vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time .
of accident 7.1.
On merits, the contents of the claim petition have been denied for want of knowledge.
8. Thus, the respondents have prayed for the of dismissal of the claim petition.

9. From the pleadings of the parties, the following rt issues were framed, by the learned Tribunal,
vide order dated 13.01.2011:
1.
Whether the petitioner was dependent upon deceased Smt. Lajja Devi, his mother?

OPP. 
2. Whether Smt. Lajja Devi, mother of the petitioner, on 14.4.2010 was travelling in Car No. HP 33B 2772 and respondent No.2 was driving Truck No. HR38L0712 rashly and negligently and near village Kalpi at about 3.30 p.m. as a result of rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2, the Truck struck with the Car and as a result Smt. Lajja Devi had died as alleged?
OPP 3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to the compensation amount, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP 4.
Whether the petition is not maintainable as alleged?
Whether respondent No.2 is registered owner of the Truck No. HR38L0712, if so, its effect?

Whether the Truck No. HR38L0712 was being plied without valid and effective Registration Certificate cum fitness Certificate and without .
valid route Permit as alleged ?
OPR.3.

Insurance Company is not maintainable as alleged?
OPR.3.
8. Whether the accident hd caused due to head on collision between Car No. HP33B2772 and of Truck No. HR38L0712 and therefore, it was the result of contributory negligence as alleged?
Whether the respondent No.2 did not hold a valid rt and effective driving licence to drive the category of vehicle as alleged?

OPR.3.
10. Relief.
10.
Thereafter, the parties to the lis were directed to adduce evidence.

11. After the closure of evidence of the parties to the lis and after hearing learned counsel for the parties, the learned Tribunal has partly allowed the petition, by passing the impugned award, as referred to above, on the ground that the petitioner is not dependent upon deceased Smt. Lajja Devi.

While holding so, the learned Tribunal has relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
in Manjuri Bera Versus Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2007 Supreme Court 1474.
12.

entities.text: Manjuri Bera Versus Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2007 Supreme Court 1474
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Feeling aggrieved from the said award, petitioner has preferred the present appeal, before this Court, mainly on the ground that the learned Tribunal has wrongly held that .
the petitioner was not dependent upon the deceased.
Elaborating his stand, it is the further case that as per the record, deceased was drawing pension of Rs.15,000/ being retired teacher.
of 13.
As per the petitioner, the learned Tribunal has wrongly held the petitioner as entitled only for compensation rt under 'no fault liability' .
14. On the basis of the above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the petition as prayed for.

15. Per contra, Mr. Vinod K. Gupta and Mr. Parneet Gupta, Advocates, have supported the impugned award, on the ground that the petitioner has miserably failed to prove his alleged dependency, upon the deceased, during her life time.
16. The controversy in the present case revolves around the fact as to whether the petitioner can be held to be dependent upon the earnings of Smt. Lajja Devi, during his life time or not.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner, when appeared in the witnessbox, as PW4, has given his age as 36 years.

He has deposed in the last sentence of the examinationinchief that his mother .
used to look after him, as well as, his house.
18. This witness has deposed that he is married and blessed with a son.
He has also deposed that he is unemployed.
He has given his educational qualification as of B.Com.
He was married in the year 2009.
He has further admitted that his wife and son are dependent upon him and rt he is looking after them.
19. The petitioner has placed on record, number of documents, but, no document has been placed on record to demonstrate that he was residing with his mother.

Had, in fact, the petitioner been dependent upon the earnings of Smt. Lajja Devi, during her lifetime, in that eventuality, the petitioner must have placed on record some documents like Copy of Pariwar Register, Ration Card etc., to demonstrate this fact.
Even, his admission qua the fact that his wife and son are dependent upon him is sufficient to conclude that the petitioner was not dependent upon the earnings of deceased Lajja Devi.

20. However, keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, as well as, the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company .
Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and in Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others, (2018) 18 SCC of 130, the petitioner is entitled for the following relief, in addition to the amount, as already awarded by the learned Tribunal: rt 1. Loss of estate = Rs.15,000/
2. Funeral expenses = Rs.15,000/
4. Loss of consortium = Rs.40,000/ Total = Rs.70,000/
21.

National Insurance Company .
Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others, (2018) 18 SCC of 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is liable to be enhanced.
22. Accordingly, the present appeal is partly allowed and the amount of compensation is enhanced.
The petitioner is held entitled for an amount of Rs.1,20,000/, along with interest @ 7.5%, from the date of filing of petition till the realization of amount.
The liability to pay the amount, is on the Insurance Company, as the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
The award passed by the learned Tribunal is modified in the above terms.
24. Memo of costs be prepared.
25. Pending application(s), if any, are also disposed of.
Record be sent back.
